title: Senior Product Manager
description:
About Motorway

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to join Motorway's Product & Engineering team. Motorway is a UK online car-selling platform connecting private sellers with ~7,500 verified dealers through online auctions. You will own a problem area end to end, in either the seller or the dealer side of the marketplace, and be accountable for the outcomes you deliver.

Building is cheaper than it has ever been. The hard part now is choosing the right thing to build. We want PMs with exceptional product sense who find the problems worth solving, back that judgement with evidence, and use the latest technology to solve them in ways that weren't possible a year ago.

What you will do

Find the problems that matter

- Identify the highest-impact problem areas by combining quantitative analysis with qualitative research, and explain clearly why they matter more than the alternatives

- See through the hundreds of good ideas to the few that will move the business and create real value for sellers and dealers

- Own outcome-based goals and metrics, not feature lists

Build with AI, in your work and in our product

- Use AI to make yourself and your team faster: automate routine PM tasks, analyse data and research quickly, and prototype or vibe code solutions to get customer feedback in days, not weeks

- Ask how each product could be built differently given what AI makes possible, and bring those ideas to your squad

- Make your team 2x more effective, not 2x busier

Deliver with rigour

- Lead a cross-functional squad of engineers, designers and data specialists from discovery through launch and measurement

- Run experiments that produce learning even when they fail, and act on what you learn

- Make clear trade-offs between customer needs, technical constraints and business priorities

Bring people with you

- Communicate the what, the why and the how clearly, through crisp, data-led documents and conversations

- Work with the people closest to you (engineering, design, data) and with execs and other business units such as Operations, Customer Support, Sales and Marketing

- Influence without authority and build alignment on difficult decisions

Requirements

- Proven experience as a product manager, with a track record of shipping products that moved meaningful business metrics, not just delivering features

- Strong product sense. You can show how you found and prioritised the right problem, and what you chose not to do

- Comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative evidence: you run user research and also query data, design experiments and interpret results yourself

- Data-oriented. You use data to understand problems, set goals and measure impact, and can debate approaches with data scientists and analysts

- AI-forward. You use AI tools regularly in your own work and have hands-on experience prototyping or building with them. You have a point of view on where AI helps and where it doesn't

- A clear, confident communicator who can work with engineers and analysts day to day and with senior leaders across the business

- Ability to move between detail and strategy without losing coherence

- Self-starter with strong ownership, a curious mindset, and the ability to build domain knowledge quickly

- Experience in marketplaces, consumer products or B2B platforms is helpful but not essential

- You're excited about changing how people buy and sell cars

Benefits

We offer a fantastic range of benefits to help you thrive:

- Hybrid work schedule with 2 days per week in our Central London office, with regular social events, office drinks and free snacks to keep you going

- Great work-life balance

- Stock options so you can share in Motorway's growth and future success

- Pension scheme to plan for your future with our provider NEST

- Strong commitment to your personal development including budget for books, courses, conferences, etc

- Opt-in comprehensive health insurance through BUPA including dental care and fitness discounts

- Cycle to work scheme, save big ££ on a new bike and accessories

- One paid volunteering day a year for you to use as you wish

- Generous parental benefits including 6 months full paid maternity leave, 4 weeks paternity leave and workplace nursery scheme... and much more!

title: Responsable d'agence F/H
description:
1958, Fondasol réalise avec succès sa première mission géotechnique.

Aujourd'hui, avec plus de 10 domaines d'expertise, le Groupe Fondasol est la référence en études et ingénierie conseil de la construction.

Géotechnique, hydrogéologie, géothermie, sites et sols pollués, géophysique, études de structures…: ses collaborateurs mutualisent leurs compétences pour aider les acteurs de la construction à bâtir durablement leurs projets.

Grâce à son actionnariat salarié majoritaire, le Groupe Fondasol continue de renforcer les synergies entre ses expertises, crée des outils digitaux innovants, décarbone ses activités…

Autant dire qu'ici, passion de son métier, engagement, évolution… sont des évidences.

Prêt à conjuguer votre leadership, votre fibre commerciale et votre expertise dans un rôle à fort impact?

Rejoignez le Groupe Fondasol pour prendre les rênes de notre future agence rennaise et participer activement à l’implantation du Groupe sur un nouveau territoire stratégique.

Votre mission : créer, structurer et développer notre présence à Rennes.

Véritable entrepreneur au sein du Groupe, vous pilotez la création complète de l’agence : développement commercial, structuration opérationnelle, recrutement progressif et représentation locale.

A la fois grand ordonnateur, gestionnaire et optimisateur, vous êtes porté par un fort esprit d’entreprendre, qui contribue activement à la bonne gestion de votre agence.

De la phase commerciale au déploiement du projet stratégique et de transformation du Groupe, vous contribuez à la chaine de valeur et à l’image de marque du Groupe Fondasol.

Vos principales missions

Vous assurez le développement commercial, en proposant l’ensemble de nos expertises et solutions innovantes (Géotechnique, Hydrogéologie, Environnement, Pathologie des Structures, etc.).

Vous êtes le garant de la qualité de la relation client et de l'acquisition de nouveaux projets.

Excellent gestionnaire, vous assurez la traduction de vos actions en performance économique, optimisant la rentabilité de vos agences

Vous êtes impliqué dans les projets stratégiques du Groupe et contribuez aux décisions clés (innovations métier, projet stratégique et de transformation du Groupe, décisions stratégiques…).

Représentez Fondasol auprès des acteurs majeurs du territoire, consolidant notre image de marque et nos partenariats.

Votre future équipe

Dans un premier temps, vous démarrez en autonomie, accompagné de près par les équipes techniques, commerciales et RH du Groupe.

Votre rôle sera ensuite de constituer et structurer votre équipe, en recrutant progressivement les talents nécessaires au développement de l’agence.

Vous bénéficierez du soutien d’un réseau national d’ingénieurs et d’experts, véritable force d’ingénierie prête à collaborer pour concrétiser nos ambitions sur le Grand Ouest.

Vos principaux alliés

Une image de marque forte, héritée de plus de 65 ans d’expertise dans les sols et les structures.

Une galaxie d’outils digitaux de pointe développés en interne, pour maximiser efficacité et qualité.

Une organisation solide en filière Ingénierie et Investigations.

Le soutien des fonctions support (technique, commercial, RH…).

Un projet d’entreprise unique, porté par un actionnariat salarié majoritaire (75 % du capital détenu par les collaborateurs).

Profil recherché

Diplômé d’une école d’ingénieur ou d’un Master en Géotechnique, Génie Civil ou Travaux Publics.

Minimum 5 ans d’expérience dans une fonction similaire (bureau d’ingénierie géotechnique, fondations spéciales…).

Excellentes capacités d’organisation, de gestion et d’analyse.

Leadership naturel, sens du collectif et qualités humaines affirmées.

Goût prononcé pour le développement, la création et l’entrepreneuriat.

Vos avantages & votre carrière

Salaire fixe + primes + participation + intéressement

Véhicule de fonction

RTT (8 à 12 jours/an)

Actionnariat salarié

Tickets restaurant, mutuelle, prévoyance

Télétravail jusqu’à 2 jours par semaine

Perspectives d’évolution (mobilités géographiques ou de poste) et accompagnement personnalisé

title: Chef de produit digital F/H
description:
LIANAKA est une filiale du Groupe Fondasol, spécialiste de l’ingénierie conseil de la construction.

Allier le meilleur des données de sols, de l’IA et de l’analyse humaine dans une plateforme technologiquement avancée, pour permettre aux porteurs de projets de construction d’anticiper les risques et de saisir les opportunités liées à l'environnement des sites de leurs projets : tel est l’engagement de LIANAKA.

Dès la recherche foncière, notre plateforme délivre aux acteurs de la construction un accès direct à une information globale, qualifiée et synthétique des risques et opportunités du sous-sol.

Chaque phase du projet est également l’opportunité d’optimiser les hypothèses techniques et les solutions de travaux.

Les bénéfices directs pour nos clients? Une fiabilité des données du sous-sol optimisée, sur les critères eau, pollution des sols, géotechnique et géothermie. Une meilleure anticipation et maitrise de leurs projets. Des décisions prises plus rapidement. Une identification immédiate des gains financiers. Une contribution à l’empreinte environnementale des projets. Le tout dans un environnement digital convivial et agile.

Soyez le pivot stratégique de notre transformation numérique : entre expertise technique et performance commerciale, portez le succès d'une solution SaaS qui révolutionne l'analyse des risques de la construction.

Le Projet

Dans le cadre de notre développement numérique, le Groupe FONDASOL a déployé une plateforme SaaS innovante LIANAKA dédiée à la modélisation et l’analyse des risques du sous-sol. Elle offre aux acteurs de la construction une information fiable, rapide et optimisée en amont de leurs projets.

Votre Mission

En tant que Chef de Produit, vous êtes le chef d'orchestre de cette solution et votre rôle est transverse :

Comprendre le terrain et l'attente de nos clients

Piloter la technique et l'évolution de la plateforme

Booster le business et la commercialisation de cet outil

title: Responsable d'activité Sites et Sols Pollués F/H
description:
1958, Fondasol réalise avec succès sa première mission géotechnique.

Aujourd'hui, avec plus de 10 domaines d'expertise, le Groupe Fondasol est la référence en études et ingénierie conseil de la construction.

Géotechnique, hydrogéologie, géothermie, sites et sols pollués, géophysique, études de structures, etc : ses collaborateurs mutualisent leurs compétences pour aider les acteurs de la construction à bâtir durablement leurs projets.

Grâce à son actionnariat salarié majoritaire, le Groupe Fondasol continue de renforcer les synergies entre ses expertises, crée des outils digitaux innovants, décarbone ses activités, etc.

Autant dire qu'ici, passion de son métier, engagement, évolution… sont des évidences.

Poste

🌱 Rejoignez un acteur engagé de la transition environnementale !

Participez activement à la reconversion des friches, à la gestion des passifs environnementaux et à la dépollution des sols et des eaux souterraines en intégrant le Département Sites et Sols Pollués du Groupe Fondasol, composé de 35 spécialistes à l’échelle nationale.

Une agence dynamique au cœur des enjeux environnementaux

Notre agence de Marseille réunit 10 collaborateurs aux profils complémentaires et à l’expertise reconnue. Vous y trouverez des équipes d'investigations terrain et bien sûr un pôle ingénierie de 7 personnes.

Vos missions au quotidien

En tant que Responsable d’Activité Sites et Sols Pollués, vous êtes garant de la bonne conduite des projets SSP le territoire, de la gestion de votre équipe et du développement de l’activité. Votre territoire s'étend de Montpellier à Nice. Vous évoluez dans un environnement stimulant et multidisciplinaire, avec un fort ancrage local et un appui national.

1- Encadrement et coordination :

Superviser une équipe aujourd'hui constituée de 2 ingénieurs Sites et Sols Pollués et d'un technicien , en assurant leur accompagnement et leur développement technique.

Faire grandir votre équipe en favorisant le partage de connaissances, la montée en compétences ainsi que leur bien-être.

Collaborer étroitement avec les autres expertises métiers de l'agence et du territoire.

2- Développement commercial :

Participer activement au développement de l'activité Sites et Sols Pollués de l'agence et du Département et assurer la relation client (promoteurs, industriels, collectivités, etc.)

Répondre aux appels d’offres et contribuer à la visibilité du Groupe sur votre territoire,

Optimiser le plan de charge de votre équipe et la rentabilité de l’activité.

3- Gestion de projets techniques :

Affaires courantes : apporter votre expertise technique tout au long de la vie d’un projet (phase étude, conception ou suivi de travaux) dans le cadre de projets d’aménagement impliquant un diagnostic de pollution des sols comme par exemple :

La reconstitution du passif environnemental

L'évaluation de la qualité des milieux, des risques sanitaires et la mise en compatibilité du projet

La définition des mesures de gestion et maitrise des risques

La surveillance environnementale

Projets complexes : jouer le rôle de chef de projet en faisant appel à des ressources techniques multiples du groupe afin de répondre au mieux aux besoins de nos clients

Stratégiques et innovations : contribuez au projet stratégique et de transformation du Groupe (innovations métier, innovations techniques, décisions stratégiques, etc.)

Votre profil

Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme d'Ingénieur ou d'un Master spécialisé en Sites et Sols Pollués, Géologie, Hydrogéologie,

Vous justifiez d'une expérience en management d'équipes techniques d'au minimum 4 ans,

Vous avez un profil commercial et êtes à l'aise avec l'approche client,

Vous avez une bonne connaissance des outils de modélisation et les logiciels spécifiques au métier,

Votre rigueur, votre esprit d'analyse et vos qualités de leader sont vos principaux atouts pour accompagner vos équipes et vos clients,

Le permis B est indispensable pour vos déplacements sur les chantiers et chez les clients.

Avantages

Véhicule de fonction

Télétravail jusqu'à 2 jours par semaine

RTT (8 à 10 jours/an)

Participation et intéressement

Actionnariat salarié

Prime de vacances

Prime sur objectifs

Tickets restaurant

Mutuelle familiale

Prévoyance

Plan de formation dynamique

Mobilité interne

Ce que nous vous offrons

La possibilité d’intégrer un Groupe novateur (Foreuse électrique Cléa, Solscore, Lianaka…) et en pleine croissance, où l'expertise Sites et Sols Pollués est un pilier de notre développement

Un environnement de travail stimulant, collaboratif et riche en expertises

Des formations techniques et des perspectives d’évolution professionnelle

Une rémunération attractive selon votre expérience et vos compétences

La possibilité de vous investir localement, régionalement, voir à l’international pour des missions d’expertise ponctuelles

title: Senior SecOps Team Lead
description:
Equativ is an independent ad tech company. Our programmatic advertising platform runs at high scale, with production running entirely on Google Cloud Platform. Equativ is building its ISMS toward ISO 27001 certification target by the end of 2027. The SecOps team secures that platform and works with every team across Equativ.

The role
You manage the SecOps team and own the day-to-day security operations of a full-cloud company. You build the team, grow its people and deliver the SecOps roadmap, which you define with the IT & Security lead.

You stay close to the technology: roughly 30% of your time is spent on people management and stakeholders, 70% on technical leadership and hands-on work during incidents and key projects.

Responsibilities
People and team

Manage the SecOps engineers: 1:1s, objectives, annual reviews, CPF level assessments and career growth.

Run the team's rituals, plan and prioritize the SEC Jira backlog.

Represent SecOps in cross-team forums with R&D and Operations teams.

Report security operations KPIs and risks to the IT & Security lead.

Security operations

Define and enforce the GCP security baseline: organization policies, IAM and service-account hygiene, VPC Service Controls, KMS and Secret Manager.

Own cloud security posture with Wiz, and drive remediation with owning teams.

Own detection and response: log pipelines, SIEM use cases, alert quality, incident playbooks.

Lead security incidents end-to-end and run blameless post-mortems.

Run vulnerability management across cloud, containers, dependencies and external attack surface; track remediation SLAs.

Scope external pentests and follow findings through to remediation.

Embed security in the SDLC with R&D: threat modeling, SAST, SCA, secret and container scanning.

Own the operational evidence for the ISMS and ISO 27001 audit

Own the technical answers to security questionnaires and RFPs.

Must-have profile

8+ years in security engineering or SecOps, including 3+ years securing production on a public cloud — GCP strongly preferred, AWS/Azure transferable.

2+ years managing a security team: hiring, reviews, coaching.

Strong GCP security knowledge: IAM model, org policies, VPC-SC, logging, GKE security.

Hands-on experience with modern cloud-native security platforms such as Google SecOps (Chronicle), Security Command Center (SCC), and Wiz (or similar CNAPPs).

Proven incident response leadership, including cloud incidents.

Experience running detection, vulnerability management and pentest programs.

Able to set priorities, say no and arbitrate between security risk and delivery.

Clear written and spoken English and French; able to explain risk to engineers, leadership and customers.

Nice to have

Kubernetes / GKE hardening and runtime security.

Experience in ad tech or other high-throughput, latency-sensitive platforms.

Exposure to ISO 27001 or SOC 2 audits from the operations side.

Identity and endpoint stack: Okta, Google Workspace, CrowdStrike.

Certifications: GCP Professional Cloud Security Engineer, CISSP, GCIH.

title: Sr. Channel Account Executive
description:
Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Sr. Channel Account Executive, you will be tasked with managing an assigned group of focus partners in the French region where we are rapidly growing our presence and revenues. This role will report into the Senior Director, Channels SEUR. You will manage existing and grow new national focus partners that will allow better market and vertical sales and support coverage

What will you do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Implement and manage an effective channel strategy
  • Increase Partner Generated revenues and Partner Initiated Deals
  • Manage existing and grow new national focus partners that will allow better market and vertical sales and support coverage
  • Execute account mapping, meetings and demand generation activities with other SentinelOne staff and partners to qualify target accounts and opportunities that will lead to Partner Initiated Deals and POCs
  • Generate monthly, quarterly and yearly planning of sales activities 
  • Lead Enablement sessions to train our focus partners to ensure we have self-sufficient partners
  • Build up strong relationships with relevant decision makers and key persons within partners
  • Support marketing plans and coordination of marketing activities

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • 5+ years of high-tech channel sales experience in an enterprise sales environment, with experience of both resell and MSSP sales motion
  • Proven track-record of driving continued partner growth and revenue
  • Knowledge of and network within leading French VAR partners 
  • Understands business models of channel partners and knows how to build in our solutions and offerings into Partner offerings
  • Strong working knowledge of the cyber security or similar space
  • Metrics driven and accountable - takes ownership and responsibility
  • Can work in a fast paced, start-up environment
  • Great relation and reputation with key partners in assigned region
  • Able to present in front of a bigger audience and to host events with and for partners and end-customers
  • Able to identify and initiate deals with partners
  • Able to work on deals and close them with a partner in close sync with SentinelOne Account Teams
  • Fluent French and English
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience

Why us?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family:

Equity & Rewards

  • Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

Time Off & Wellbeing

  • Competitive leave benefits
  • Gender-neutral parental leave

Insurance & Financial Security

  • Medical and insurance benefits
  • Disability insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Work Perks & Flexibility

  • Global home office allowance

title: DevOps, Core Platform
description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the role

We are building software infrastructure to power AI development and delivery for operational use cases in defense. Our software needs to run in customers' data centers, on their hardware, often with no internet connection. You will own the continuous deployment of our software in these environments. That covers installations, upgrades with no downtime, and keeping track of dependencies between the services that make up the software.

This role involves hands-on coding. You will join the core platform team, with broad ownership and a direct effect on real defense deployments.

Responsibilities

Delivery: Take a change from a commit in CI to a running system on a customer site, and keep every step repeatable.

Safe upgrades: Roll out upgrades step by step with no downtime, watch the system as it changes, and stop and alert the team automatically when something goes wrong.

Disconnected sites: Make installs and upgrades work with no internet, using signed, self-contained packages.

Release checks: Work on the release system that checks that all our services work together, in CI and at release time.

Collaboration: Work with platform architects and developers so every new service is easy to package, deploy and upgrade. Work with our forward deployed engineers, who install and run the software at customer sites, so the same tools run in development and at the customer.

Documentation: Write the procedures that a person at a customer site can follow without our help.

Growth: Make it easier and faster for our engineers to ship changes to customer sites.

Candidate requirements

Experience: Several years of backend or infrastructure engineering, ideally on a product with many services and many deployments.

Coding: Strong skills in at least one language (Rust, Go, Python, Java).

Kubernetes and delivery: Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and containers, and with Helm, GitOps (Argo CD or Flux) and CI systems.

Builder: You have built, not just used, tools that deploy or run software.

Production: You have run or debugged upgrades or deployments in production, and you know the basics of metrics, health checks and logs.

Educational background: Degree in computer science, software engineering or a similar field. Equivalent professional experience is equally valued.

Language: Clear written and spoken English.

Nice to have

Writing Kubernetes operators or controllers.

Signing and supply-chain tools, such as Sigstore/cosign and SBOMs.

Packaging software for air-gapped sites, for example with Zarf and registry mirrors such as Harbor.

Bare-metal Kubernetes (OpenShift, RKE2 or Talos) with Ceph or MinIO.

Mindset

Pragmatic engineering: You choose simple solutions and proven tools first.

Attention to detail: You obsess over edge cases and robustness before you ship a change.

User-oriented: You treat other engineers as your users. You take care designing APIs and tools that are simple and pleasant to use.

Ownership: You take responsibility for ensuring the project works regardless of your job description.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Navigation Engineer (Precise Navigation)
description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As a Navigation Engineer within our Precise Navigation team, you will design and develop high-precision navigation and positioning solutions based on tightly-coupled IMU/GNSS filtering, improving localisation accuracy, integrity, and robustness to jamming and spoofing for our autonomous systems – from concept to field deployment. You will work hand-in-hand with the Navigation and Radar teams, as well as software and Electronic Warfare (EW) teams, to deliver robust, resilient Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) and ensure overall performance, robustness and reliability.

Responsibilities

Navigation Architecture: Drive the architecture and implementation of navigation / PNT solutions for autonomous platforms.

Resilient PNT: Develop navigation resilient to GNSS degradation, jamming and spoofing (anti-jam / anti-spoof).

Sensor Fusion: Design multi-sensor fusion (GNSS, INS/IMU, RF, vision) and the associated estimation and filtering algorithms.

Testing & Validation: Design test plans (e.g. GNSS receiver testing in jamming environments), run simulations and replays, and report on findings and performance against targets.

Technical Coordination: Collaborate across HW, software, EW and ML teams on technical interfaces and system-level trade-offs.

System Reviews & Documentation: Contribute to design and architecture reviews and maintain requirements traceability and documentation.

Candidate Requirements

MSc in Engineering (aerospace, robotics, EE or related); PhD is a plus.

Strong mathematical background combined with good physical intuition.

Experience with GNSS, INS/IMU and navigation/estimation filters (e.g. Kalman filtering), particularly in tightly-coupled architectures.

Experience with navigation in GNSS-denied / contested environments.

Familiarity with RF and EW constraints (GNSS jamming / spoofing) is a plus.

Solid software / algorithm skills; combined algo + software profile rather than a pure coder.

Broad engineering culture with understanding of electrical, embedded and mechanical systems.

Rigorous, structured and mission-driven mindset with strong analytical skills.

Excellent communication and documentation abilities.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Team

We are looking for a Growth Strategy & Monetization Manager to join the Ad Monetization team. You will work directly on revenue-critical topics, combining strategic thinking, data-driven analysis, and operational execution to improve performance across millions of daily users. This role is ideal for someone with a consulting or analytical background who wants to move from advising to owning a € multi-hundred-million revenue engine.

Drive revenue Performance

Own ad monetization performance across a portfolio of games and apps

Analyze revenue drivers such as ARPDAU, fill rate, eCPM, LTV, and ad engagement

Identify structural improvement levers across waterfall configuration, in-app bidding, pricing strategy, and demand diversification

Translate analysis into concrete action plans with measurable revenue impact

Optimize the ad tech stack

Structure and lead A/B tests to maximize yield and long-term LTV

Evaluate and integrate new ad networks, bidding partners, and ad monetization formats

Act as a business owner

Take ownership of initiatives end-to-end, from diagnosis to implementation

title: Développeur Python IA
description:
Développeur Python IA (H/F)

Paris/Lille | Secteur Assurance

Pourquoi cette opportunité ?

Parce que vous participerez à la construction de notre stratégie d’intelligence artificielle, que nous sommes en train de définir.
Vous rejoindrez une équipe motivée et talentueuse, dont la mission est d’intégrer l’IA au cœur de nos processus métier.

L’objectif est de répondre aux besoins de nos équipes comme à ceux de nos clients, et d’automatiser certaines tâches à faible valeur ajoutée.

Éléments clés

Concevoir des solutions RAG et agentiques appliquées à des cas d’usage métier concrets.
Développer et orchestrer des agents tout en assurant la traçabilité des sources et la maîtrise des hallucinations.
Contribuer directement au workflow de paramétrage produit KELIA, avec une validation humaine intégrée aux étapes clés.
Participer à la mise en production des assistants, de leur API jusqu’à leur intégration dans l’interface web interne.

Ce qu’il faut savoir :

Nous recherchons un(e) Développeur Python IA pour rejoindre notre équipe R&D à Paris ou Lille

Vous interviendrez sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie des solutions, de la conception jusqu’à la mise en production, en mobilisant différentes approches : modèles de langage (LLM), apprentissage supervisé, clustering et autres techniques de machine Learning.

Un volet important de la mission concerne également le paramétrage produit : l’objectif est d’extraire les informations pertinentes des conditions générales, de proposer un paramétrage, de prévoir une validation par un expert à chaque étape et de produire un fichier directement importable dans KELIA.

Missions principales :

Vous développez en Python des fonctionnalités IA.

Ingestion documentaire : extraire le texte et les tableaux des PDF, des pages Confluence, des documents SharePoint et des dépôts GitLab, puis découper, indexer et mettre à jour ces contenus avec des jobs asynchrones.
Recherche : recherche hybride (sémantique et mots-clés), filtres par collection et par chemin, reranking, et recherche visuelle sur les pages de documents.
Agents et LLM : développer des agents avec LangGraph (routage, recherche, filtrage, réflexion, réponse), écrire et versionner les prompts, citer les sources, et répondre « je ne trouve pas » quand l'information manque.
Workflow de paramétrage produit : contribuer à l'agent qui extrait les informations des conditions générales, propose le paramétrage, fait valider chaque étape par un expert et produit un fichier importable dans KELIA.
Qualité : maintenir des jeux de tests, mesurer le taux de bonnes réponses, suivre les réponses inventées et vérifier que les résultats sont stables d'un run à l'autre.
Coût et latence : suivre la consommation de tokens, le temps de première réponse et le cache, et choisir le bon modèle pour chaque tâche.
API : exposer les assistants en API, avec des réponses en streaming, et les intégrer à l'interface web interne.
Documenter votre code, écrire des tests et participer aux revues de code.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si:

Vous êtes diplômé(e) d’un Bac+5 en informatique ou assurance
Vous maîtrisez Python 3.11+ et êtes à l’aise avec le développement d’API via FastAPI, Pydantic et le streaming SSE.
Vous avez une expérience ou un réel intérêt pour les solutions d’IA générative, les LLM et les architectures agentiques avec LangChain, LangGraph et LiteLLM.
Vous connaissez les principes de RAG, de recherche hybride, d’embeddings et de reranking, idéalement avec Qdrant.
Vous savez travailler avec des sources documentaires variées et leur ingestion, notamment des PDF, Confluence, SharePoint ou GitLab, avec des outils tels que Docling.
Vous êtes à l’aise avec les environnements de stockage et de persistance reposant sur PostgreSQL et le stockage objet S3.
Vous accordez de l’importance à l’observabilité et à la qualité des solutions IA, notamment au suivi des prompts, des traces, des logs, des coûts et des performances, avec des outils comme MLflow.
Vous êtes sensibilisé aux enjeux de sécurité, d’authentification et de gestion des rôles, notamment avec Keycloak.
Vous évoluez avec aisance dans un environnement d’industrialisation moderne utilisant Git, GitLab CI, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm et pytest, ainsi que des outils collaboratifs comme Jira et Confluence.

Ce que vous apportez

Une bonne maîtrise de Python et de ses bonnes pratiques : tests (pytest), typage, gestion des dépendances.
Votre expérience dans l’utilisation des API de LLM et bases du prompt engineering, y compris les sorties structurées.
Votre compréhension du fonctionnement d'un RAG : embeddings, découpage, recherche, génération.
Une bonne maîtrise du SQL et notions de bases de données.
Git et travail en équipe.

Pourquoi nous joindre:

Pour contribuer à une stratégie où l’intelligence artificielle est un levier clé de la feuille de route technologique, avec des solutions intégrées au cœur des outils métiers.
Pour travailler sur des cas d’usage concrets d’IA générative, de RAG et d’agents LLM, de l’expérimentation jusqu’à l’industrialisation.
Pour associer des technologies IA de pointe à une expertise métier forte dans le secteur de l’assurance et créer des solutions à impact réel.

Prêt(e) à démarrer une nouvelle expérience ?
Envoyez-nous votre candidature et commençons la conversation

title: Technicien Infrastructures Réseaux (H/F)
description:
Nous recrutons pour la durée. Ce poste est un CDI, avec des horaires fixes, des missions planifiées à l’avance et un lieu d’attache unique. Nous cherchons quelqu’un qui veut s’installer durablement chez Azurreo, pas un poste de passage.

À propos d’Azurreo

Azurreo est la branche télécommunications et technologies de Seelon Holdings, groupe d’investissement international présent sur quatre continents. Notre plateforme SignalVerify mesure la qualité de service et la qualité d’expérience des réseaux dans plus de 144 pays. Depuis plus de quinze ans, nous accompagnons opérateurs, intégrateurs et constructeurs en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique, avec plus de 250 projets livrés dans plus de 25 pays. Azurreo exploite aussi sa propre infrastructure réseaux et télécoms.

Le poste

Vous préparez, installez et raccordez la couche physique de notre infrastructure : câblage cuivre et fibre optique, baies, équipements. Au quotidien, vous travaillez depuis notre bureau de Croissy-sur-Seine, où vous préparez le matériel et participez aux expéditions. Vous partez en mission en France et à l’étranger pour les installations sur site. Ces missions sont planifiées à l’avance et coordonnées avec vous.

La stabilité, au cœur du poste

Un CDI, pour construire dans la durée

Des horaires fixes, du lundi au vendredi

Des missions planifiées à l’avance et coordonnées avec vous

Un lieu d’attache unique, Croissy-sur-Seine, où vous retrouvez votre équipe et votre matériel

Un accompagnement à l’arrivée, puis une formation continue

Une entreprise présente depuis plus de quinze ans, dans plus de 25 pays

Missions principales

Câblage et fibre optique

Tirage, raccordement, brassage, repérage et étiquetage de câbles cuivre (RJ45) et fibre optique

Tests et contrôles des liaisons, puis mise en service

Installation en baie

Installation et raccordement de baies informatiques

Montage d’équipements (rack & stack) et mise en place des câblages associés

Matériel et expéditions

Préparation et contrôle du matériel avant expédition

Participation à la réception et à l’envoi des colis

Suivi des stocks, des inventaires et du matériel confié

Missions sur site

Installation et mise en service sur nos sites, en France et à l’international

Diagnostic des pannes physiques, maintenance préventive et corrective

Comptes-rendus d’intervention et mise à jour des tickets

Respect des procédures qualité et sécurité d’Azurreo et des consignes de chaque site

Profil recherché

Indispensable

Un projet à long terme : vous cherchez un poste dans la durée, pas une étape courte

Une première expérience en fibre optique et en câblage (raccordement, installation, déploiement)

Résider en France

Permis B en cours de validité

Disponibilité pour des missions en France et à l’international, planifiées à l’avance

Français courant et anglais niveau A2 minimum, pour lire la documentation technique et échanger avec nos équipes à l’étranger

Rigueur, organisation et travail soigné et documenté

Un atout majeur

Soudure de fibre optique et mesures optiques

Également apprécié

Installation en baie ou en datacenter

Notions de réseau (TCP/IP, VLAN) et connaissance d’équipements Cisco, Huawei, Aruba, Fortinet ou Juniper

Habilitations et certifications : AIPR, habilitation électrique, travail en hauteur, CACES nacelle, SST

Il vous manque une habilitation ou une certification ? Nous organisons la formation.

Formation : Bac Pro SN, BTS SIO, BTS CIEL, BTS Télécommunications, BUT/DUT Réseaux & Télécommunications, Licence professionnelle Réseaux, ou expérience équivalente.

Ce que nous offrons

Un CDI, avec une période d’essai de 3 mois renouvelable une fois d’un commun accord

39 heures par semaine, du lundi au vendredi

Une couverture santé

Une prime liée à la performance

25 jours de congés payés

Des heures supplémentaires compensées en temps de repos

Des frais professionnels avancés par l’entreprise

Une formation aux certifications et habilitations qui vous manquent

Un accompagnement à l’arrivée et une formation continue

Un travail varié : atelier, installation et missions à l’étranger

Comment candidater

Envoyez-nous votre CV, avec quelques lignes sur une intervention dont vous êtes fier : ce qu’il y avait à faire, ce qui a coincé, comment vous l’avez réglé. Dites-nous aussi ce que vous cherchez pour les prochaines années.

Le processus comprend un entretien RH, un entretien avec votre futur manager et un entretien final avec Adam Anbari, gérant d’Azurreo EURL. L’embauche est conditionnée à une visite médicale d’aptitude au poste.

Azurreo étudie toutes les candidatures à compétences égales, sans distinction d’origine, de sexe, d’âge, de situation personnelle ou de handicap.

Le stage se déroulera au sein du Pôle Qualité de Vie et Conditions de Travail à la direction des Ressources Humaines de Handicap International, avec un démarrage mi-janvier pour une durée de 6 mois. Le pôle est constitué d’une référente santé/handicap et d’une manager QVCT/prévention des risques psycho sociaux. Phase 3 : réalisation de supports de communication interne variés en français et anglais ; co élaboration d’un e-learning simple et synthétique sur les addictions et leur prévention

title: Embedded Linux Engineer (Yocto Specialist)
description:
About Genesis

Genesis is a physical AI lab and full-stack robotics company building general-purpose robots, with teams in Paris and the Bay Area. Our people have built some of the most widely used platforms in robotics research including the open-source Genesis simulator, pioneered generative simulation and led foundation-model work at some of the world's leading AI labs. We own the whole stack: hardware, embedded systems, simulation, data and robot foundation models.

The Role

Every Genesis robot runs on a custom jetson thor compute board and every piece of software we write: control, perception, learned policies, depends on the Linux image underneath it. We are looking for a senior engineer to own that image end to end: build it, ship it to the robot, keep it updatable, and make it easy for the rest of the team to compile and deploy on top of it.

This is an in-house ownership role. You will be the reference for embedded Linux at Genesis, working closely with our embedded, robotics and application-software engineers in Paris and with our hardware partners. The job is to provide a reliable, well maintained and up to date os image, customized to our needs.

What You'll Do

Build, own and maintain the production Yocto/OpenEmbedded distribution for our robot's custom board: BSP, kernel, device tree, rootfs, toolchain and custom layers.

Bring up new hardware on NVIDIA Jetson-class platforms, integrating drivers and peripherals. Including hands-on debugging of components such as Wi-Fi, cameras, audio devices and buses on the physical robot.

Own the full image lifecycle: reproducible builds, versioned releases, secure and robust over-the-air (OTA) updates, and long-term maintenance as hardware and software evolve.

Deliver a development kit and workflow (SDK, cross-compilation, deployment tooling) so engineers can build and ship their software onto the robot quickly.

Integrate GPU and AI-accelerator inference stacks so that our models run efficiently on the robot.

Speed up the team's build and CI pipeline for image generation and validation. Builds are long, so caching and automation matter, as well as removing unnecessary dependencies.

Document the system and make it approachable, so the image is never again a black box that only one person (or contractor) understands.

Your First Three Months

Build a custom Yocto image for the robot's custom boards.

Flash, boot and validate it on real hardware, working through driver and integration issues on-site.

Set up the cross compilation workflow, caching, CI automations to streamline the robotics team work

What You'll Bring

Passion for your craft and demonstrated excellence in embedded Linux engineering.

5+ years of hands-on embedded Linux experience, including shipping at least one Yocto-based image to production not only a prototype.

Proven ownership of an image through its lifecycle: maintenance, release management and remote/OTA updates.

Deep experience with Yocto internals: layers, recipes, BitBake, machine and distro configuration, SDK generation.

Strong board bring-up and low-level debugging skills: kernel configuration, device trees, drivers, boot chain.

Hands-on experience with the NVIDIA Jetson family (JetPack / L4T, meta-tegra) or comparable embedded GPU platforms.

Knowledge C++ and Python packaging systems and how to deal with cross-compilation.

The ability to explain how your work fits into the wider build, development and deployment system.

Exceptional ownership and initiative, with the judgment to choose workable solutions for our current stage over the theoretically ideal one.

Bonus

Experience integrating GPU / AI-accelerator inference (CUDA, TensorRT or similar) on embedded targets.

Background in robotics, drones, connected devices or other products with custom hardware.

Experience working with chip vendors or ODMs.

Familiarity with secure boot, real-time kernel tuning (PREEMPT_RT) or OTA frameworks such as Mender, RAUC or SWUpdate.

French and English. Mandarin is a plus.

You'll Thrive Here If You

Enjoy being the go-to person for a critical system and making it easier for others to use.

Unblock teammates' requests quickly and pragmatically, and know when "good enough to ship" is the right answer.

Stay patient and methodical when a single build takes two hours and a bug only shows up on hardware.

Like startup flexibility: changing priorities, short feedback loops and work that ranges from kernel to tooling.

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
description:
What Quadrants is

Quadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.

The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.

It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.

The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.

The role

You own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.

Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.

It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.

The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.

Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime.

What you’ll own

API & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. title: Genesis-World: Core Physics Engineer
description:
What we're building

Robots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future.

Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI. One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available (paper). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact (paper) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise.

Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.

This is at the core of Genesis AI's strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

You push the physics of Genesis-World forward. The mandate is clear: ship production-ready simulation capabilities that matter for the company's internal needs. Research applied end-to-end, from algorithm to merged, tested, documented code that real robot-learning pipelines depend on. Occasional groundbreaking research happens, notably through academic collaborations. But the core of the job is making the engine measurably better along five axes:

Speed. Algorithms that are not only faster but also smart enough to spend compute only where it matters across both time and space: larger stable timesteps, selective fidelity (adaptive across scales or simply hand-set), structure-aware solvers.

Completeness. No physics off limits: water, human animation, air flow, gravel, tendons, even body organs. Whatever the next use-case needs, the engine grows to cover it.

Fidelity. More realistic models: contact, friction, deformation, energy, actuation, materials…

Versatility. Extensible multi-physics without compromise on realism: all solvers in the scene coupled together at once, two-way and constraint-based. Write your own solver and it joins the scene like a native one, growing into an open solver ecosystem.

Scalability. From workstation to factory scale, and one day, city scale: thousands of interacting entities, batched across environments, without losing physical soundness.

Our ambition is to establish Genesis-World as the go-to simulator for physical AI, from companies and research labs to individuals.

The problems waiting for you

Every fidelity for every physics. The same physics at every point of the speed-accuracy spectrum, from heavily batched training with XPBD or VBD to final validation with IPC. Same scene, same API, pick your tradeoff.

Invent physics level-of-detail (LOD). Rendering has had LOD for decades, physics is still waiting. Simulate at full fidelity what agents interact with and see, coarsely what they do not.

Heterogeneous environments. Every parallel world can hold a completely different model: different bodies, joints, and collision geometries.

Adaptive timesteps per island. Error-based control with Runge-Kutta Dopri5, and Time-of-Impact stepping during collision detection, as done in Jiminy.

Couple everything, exactly. Efficient and accurate two-way constraint-based coupling between heterogeneous grey-box solvers, using state-of-the-art methods like ADMM. Owning every solver in the stack is what makes it possible.

More scalable constraint solvers. Push rigid constraint solving beyond its current scalability ceiling (reference).

Unify contact resolution. Hydro-elastic compliance, unilateral constraints, and sequential impulses in the same framework, ideally under one generic formulation.

Closed kinematic loops without constraints. Handle loops intrinsically for numerical stability and speed, in the spirit of Kamino.

Day to day: you write your physics in plain Python and Quadrants makes it fast on every backend. And you validate it the hard way: analytical closed forms, other engines, real-world data.

Who you are

You are a physicist and an engineer at once. You judge a method by whether it holds up in production at real scale, and you do not stop until it does. No blind spots: you relentlessly hunt down even the defect that looks insignificant, because it never is.

A strong background in physics-based simulation, preferably related to robotics: RBD, FEM, MPM, SPH, IPC, XPBD, VBD, ABD, plus constrained optimization and numerical integration of stiff systems.

A track record of shipping simulation code that others rely on, in an engine, in industry, or in a research codebase used beyond its authors.

Solid HPC programming (CPU and/or GPU), and an instinct for what makes a numerical method fast in practice, beyond complexity classes.

Rigor in validation: analytical closed forms, cross-engine consistency, real-world data.

Bonus points: publications in simulation, graphics, or robotics venues (SIGGRAPH, ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS). Contributions to an open-source physics engine.

description:

Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

Simulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally.

Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you.

You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture.

The problems waiting for you

Make testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams.

Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically.

Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid.

Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant.

Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on.

Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine.

Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly.

Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins.

Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay.

Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption.

Who you are

You care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. A slow test, a cryptic error, a manual step: you see it, you go after the root cause, and you remove it for everyone. You have opinions about API design.

You are comfortable with physics and robotics: the right design choices take a working picture of what a simulator like Genesis-World does, how it works, and how it is used, a picture you can partly build on the job.

Strong Python engineering on large codebases: architecture, refactoring, typing, packaging, performance profiling (py-spy, Nsight, Xcode Instruments, RenderDoc).

Developer tooling, test infrastructure, or CI at scale.

Enough fluency with JIT compilation, code generation, or GPU computing stacks to reason about compilation caching, kernel dispatch, and startup cost. You will work closely with Quadrants.

At ease debugging across the full platform matrix: Windows, Linux, and macOS, on x86 and arm64, over CUDA, AMD, and Apple Metal (and possibly Intel XPU via Vulkan soon)

Open-source reflexes: triaging issues, reviewing external pull requests, communicating with a community.

Bonus points: experience with other robotics simulators (Drake, MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac, RaiSim, Jiminy, Brax). PyTorch, our user-facing interface. Other JIT compilers such as Triton, JAX, or Numba. 3D tooling and interactive editors (Maya, Blender, Houdini). Serialization formats (USD, glTF, MJCF/URDF). C++, CUDA, or Metal. Developer relations or community work.

title: Senior AI Research Engineer - LLM Training & Inference Infrastructure
description:
As a Research Engineer on the Frontier Foundations team, you will partner with Research Scientists to build the systems that run large-scale LLM training, reinforcement learning, and inference at Datadog. You will build and operate an in-house distributed runtime that schedules work across large GPU clusters, and you will own how quickly researchers can iterate and how reliably long training runs complete. 

Building on our track record of AI-powered solutions (e.g., Bits AI, Bits Evolve, and our time series foundation model Toto), Datadog AI Research (DAIR) tackles high-risk, high-reward problems grounded in real-world challenges in cloud observability and security. 

The Frontier Foundations team builds and maintains the high-performance infrastructure that lets us train and serve large language models at scale. It supports both of our research areas: 

Trained Agents for Observability -- Post-training models to operate autonomously across Datadog's domain. SRE incident response is our first target, with a clear path to code repair, security response, and infrastructure optimization. We build the simulation environments, RL training loops, and evaluation infrastructure needed to train agents that match or surpass frontier models at a fraction of the cost. 

 

What You'll Do: 

  • Design, build, and operate distributed training and inference infrastructure for large language models, including Mixture-of-Experts models 
  • Scale training with parallelism strategies (data, tensor, pipeline, and expert), memory optimization, checkpointing, and failure recovery
  • Build inference and rollout systems that support evaluation, experimentation, and RL without slowing down training
  • Build execution environments and sandboxes for online RL and agent post-training
  • Own continuous performance validation: regular benchmarks of rollout speed, training throughput, and learning behavior, with dashboards that make regressions visible 
  • Improve the researcher experience: job submission, scheduling, quotas, GPU utilization, and observability
  • Work with platform teams on cluster capacity, networking, and scheduling across GPU providers 
  • Investigate performance and reliability problems across hardware, software, and distributed systems 

 

Who You Are:

  • You have depth in distributed systems and ML infrastructure for training and inference at scale; experience with Ray, Kubernetes, Slurm, or similar frameworks is a plus
  • You are proficient in Python and in at least one systems language (e.g., Rust, C++, or Go) ● You have experience operating large-scale training or serving infrastructure, or schedulers and orchestration systems for GPU or other high-performance workloads
  • You understand what limits throughput/latency in distributed inference workloads: communication, memory, scheduling, and stragglers
  • You have strong debugging, profiling, and incident-diagnosis skills, ideally including on-call experience 
  • You can explain design and performance trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences 
  • Prior experience training machine learning models is valuable but not essential for engineers with strong distributed systems or HPC backgrounds 

 

Bonus Points (any of the following): 

  • You are familiar with distributed training frameworks such as Megatron-LM, TorchTitan, or DeepSpeed
  • You have experience with LLM inference engines such as vLLM or SGLang, including batching and KV-cache management 
  • You have experience with RL training systems and rollout infrastructure 
  • You have experience with collective communication (NCCL), RDMA, or low-latency networking 
  • You have experience with GPU benchmarking, profiling, and cluster performance monitoring 
  • You have experience building sandboxed code execution or large-scale evaluation infrastructure 
  • You have contributed to open-source ML or distributed systems projects

What You'll Do:

  • Write, tune, and debug GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton, or similar) for the operations that dominate LLM training and inference.
  • Optimize for the latest NVIDIA GPU generations, including memory hierarchy, tensor cores, and low-precision formats such as FP8 and FP4
  • Reduce communication cost in distributed workloads (all-to-all, all-reduce) and overlap communication with compute across NVLink and across nodes
  • Profile end-to-end training and rollout workloads to identify whether they are compute-, memory-, or communication-bound, and quantify the headroom
  • Build benchmarks, profiling tools, and regression tests that guide optimization decisions

title: General Counsel at amo
description:
amo is a Paris-based consumer social company. We want to build Europe's most ambitious consumer company. Our apps Bump and Sugar are used by millions of people all over the globe.

Location sits at the heart of one of our current products, and privacy, trust and safety are part of how we build, not an afterthought.

We're scaling fast, and this comes with legal implications. We want them handled in a way that speeds the business up.

The role:

We're hiring our first General Counsel to own amo's legal function end to end. This is a business role, not a support function: you'll work directly with the cofounders, join discussions from the start and work with every team, from Product and Distribution to People, Engineering and Finance.

You'll draft, negotiate and advise yourself on the topics that matter most. For everything else, you'll build and run a network of local counsel, with the right firm for each topic and each market, and turn their advice into clear decisions for the team.

How we think about legal:

At amo, legal starts from the product, to serve our users. We're not looking for someone who applies the rules by the book, but for someone who understands what we're building and why, and finds the legal approach that makes sense for it. You'll be judged on what you enable, not on how many memos you write.

Product and users first: you join discussions early and work with the team toward the same goal: making projects to life, fast and safe.

Pragmatic on risk: you know which rules are non-negotiable, where there is room for judgement, and how much risk is worth taking for the business. You give a recommendation, not a list of risks.

Built for scale: you set up the contracts, policies and processes that enable our growth.

What you'll own:

You'll cover every legal question that comes with scaling a consumer app across markets, working with the right local counsel on each topic:

Corporate: general corporate, group structure as we expand internationally, BSPCE plans and employee liquidity operations.

Employment: French labour law across the employee lifecycle, from contracts, immigration and internal rules to terminations.

Trademarks and IP: our global trademark portfolio: filing strategy, oppositions, watch services and disputes. Patents and content licensing as they come.

Compliance and data protection: GDPR, protection of minors, DSA, app store policies, and more. Regulator and law enforcement requests.

Commercial contracts: vendors and SaaS, partnerships, creator and influencer agreements, advertising, data processing agreements. Templates and a self-serve process so teams can move autonomously.

Litigation: pre-litigation and litigation across jurisdictions, with outside counsel. Clear risk assessments and options for the cofounders.

M&A: acquisitions and strategic transactions when the time comes, including due diligence, structuring and integration.

What success looks like:

Teams ship features, sign deals and expand without waiting on legal.

The cofounders spend far less time on legal: topics get tracked, briefed and closed without one of them driving each one, and nothing is discovered late.

The right local counsel is in place for each topic and market, on a budget we control.

What we're looking for:

Startup and scaleup experience, at our stage and beyond. 7+ years of legal experience, including a senior in-house role (General Counsel, Deputy GC or Head of Legal) at a tech company. You've lived the stage we're at international expansion, fast growth.

Expert in French and EU law. French legal training, with deep knowledge of French corporate and employment law, GDPR and EU digital regulation. Admission to the bar (CAPA) is a plus.

Global outlook. You've handled matters in several jurisdictions and know how to find, brief and challenge the right local counsel for each topic and market.

A true generalist. You move from a vendor contract negotiation to a trademark opposition in the same day, and know when to go deep yourself and when to bring in a specialist.

Product and business first. You adapt the legal approach to what the product and the business need, and give clear recommendations in plain language. You help the team move fast without taking blind risks.

Hands-on. You draft and negotiate yourself and don't need a team to get things done.

Fluent in French and English.

Comfortable with little structure. You set your own priorities in a noisy environment and would rather be judged on what you enabled than on how busy you were.

Discretion. You handle sensitive matters, including disputes, with complete confidentiality.

Nice to have:

Experience at a consumer app, social or gaming company.

Hands-on work with GDPR, content moderation (DSA).

M&A transactions led or closed, buy side or sell side.

A few years at a top-tier law firm before going in-house.

Exposure to a crisis, whether regulatory, press or security.

Why join:

You'll build the function from the ground up, with a seat next to the cofounders on the decisions that shape the company and a direct impact on the trajectory of a company that serves users all over the globe.

Life at amo:

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week.

We wanted to make sure coming to the office was as comfortable as possible for you:

We chose a location in central Paris, near Opera (Metro lines 3,8,9 and RER A).

We have a beautiful Parisian-style office with high ceilings, balconies, and huge windows. So a lot of natural light!

Because life outside of work should also be stress-free, we cover:

Health care (100% coverage).

Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Second Parent Leave (salary maintained at 100%).

Vacation days: 8-9 weeks (total) per year - (European summer? 🥹😎).

5 weeks of paid time off (by the state);

1-2 additional weeks (RTT, based on our company contract);

~11 bank holidays.

We shut down entirely twice a year, two weeks in summer and one week in winter to allow everyone to truly recharge and to avoid prolonged slowdowns (especially in the summer). These pauses are part of your total vacation time, giving everyone a real chance to unplug and recharge. No Slack, no email, no FOMO.

raw.description:
amo is a Paris-based consumer social company. We want to build Europe's most ambitious consumer company. Our apps Bump and Sugar are used by millions of people all over the globe.

Location sits at the heart of one of our current products, and privacy, trust and safety are part of how we build, not an afterthought.

We're scaling fast, and this comes with legal implications. We want them handled in a way that speeds the business up.

The role:

We're hiring our first General Counsel to own amo's legal function end to end. This is a business role, not a support function: you'll work directly with the cofounders, join discussions from the start and work with every team, from Product and Distribution to People, Engineering and Finance.

You'll draft, negotiate and advise yourself on the topics that matter most. For everything else, you'll build and run a network of local counsel, with the right firm for each topic and each market, and turn their advice into clear decisions for the team.

How we think about legal:

At amo, legal starts from the product, to serve our users. We're not looking for someone who applies the rules by the book, but for someone who understands what we're building and why, and finds the legal approach that makes sense for it. You'll be judged on what you enable, not on how many memos you write.

  • Product and users first: you join discussions early and work with the team toward the same goal: making projects to life, fast and safe.

  • Pragmatic on risk: you know which rules are non-negotiable, where there is room for judgement, and how much risk is worth taking for the business. You give a recommendation, not a list of risks.

  • Built for scale: you set up the contracts, policies and processes that enable our growth.

What you'll own:

You'll cover every legal question that comes with scaling a consumer app across markets, working with the right local counsel on each topic:

  • Corporate: general corporate, group structure as we expand internationally, BSPCE plans and employee liquidity operations.

  • Employment: French labour law across the employee lifecycle, from contracts, immigration and internal rules to terminations.

  • Trademarks and IP: our global trademark portfolio: filing strategy, oppositions, watch services and disputes. Patents and content licensing as they come.

  • Compliance and data protection: GDPR, protection of minors, DSA, app store policies, and more. Regulator and law enforcement requests.

  • Commercial contracts: vendors and SaaS, partnerships, creator and influencer agreements, advertising, data processing agreements. Templates and a self-serve process so teams can move autonomously.

  • Litigation: pre-litigation and litigation across jurisdictions, with outside counsel. Clear risk assessments and options for the cofounders.

  • M&A: acquisitions and strategic transactions when the time comes, including due diligence, structuring and integration.

What success looks like:

  • Teams ship features, sign deals and expand without waiting on legal.

  • The cofounders spend far less time on legal: topics get tracked, briefed and closed without one of them driving each one, and nothing is discovered late.

  • The right local counsel is in place for each topic and market, on a budget we control.

What we're looking for:

  • Startup and scaleup experience, at our stage and beyond. 7+ years of legal experience, including a senior in-house role (General Counsel, Deputy GC or Head of Legal) at a tech company. You've lived the stage we're at international expansion, fast growth.

  • Expert in French and EU law. French legal training, with deep knowledge of French corporate and employment law, GDPR and EU digital regulation. Admission to the bar (CAPA) is a plus.

  • Global outlook. You've handled matters in several jurisdictions and know how to find, brief and challenge the right local counsel for each topic and market.

  • A true generalist. You move from a vendor contract negotiation to a trademark opposition in the same day, and know when to go deep yourself and when to bring in a specialist.

  • Product and business first. You adapt the legal approach to what the product and the business need, and give clear recommendations in plain language. You help the team move fast without taking blind risks.

  • Hands-on. You draft and negotiate yourself and don't need a team to get things done.

  • Fluent in French and English.

  • Comfortable with little structure. You set your own priorities in a noisy environment and would rather be judged on what you enabled than on how busy you were.

  • Discretion. You handle sensitive matters, including disputes, with complete confidentiality.

Nice to have:

  • Experience at a consumer app, social or gaming company.

  • Hands-on work with GDPR, content moderation (DSA).

  • M&A transactions led or closed, buy side or sell side.

  • A few years at a top-tier law firm before going in-house.

  • Exposure to a crisis, whether regulatory, press or security.

Why join:

You'll build the function from the ground up, with a seat next to the cofounders on the decisions that shape the company and a direct impact on the trajectory of a company that serves users all over the globe.

Life at amo:

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week.

 

We wanted to make sure coming to the office was as comfortable as possible for you:

  • We chose a location in central Paris, near Opera (Metro lines 3,8,9 and RER A).

  • We have a beautiful Parisian-style office with high ceilings, balconies, and huge windows. So a lot of natural light!

 

Because life outside of work should also be stress-free, we cover:

  • Health care (100% coverage).

  • Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, Second Parent Leave (salary maintained at 100%).

  • Vacation days: 8-9 weeks (total) per year - (European summer? 🥹😎).

    • 5 weeks of paid time off (by the state);

    • 1-2 additional weeks (RTT, based on our company contract);

    • ~11 bank holidays.

      We shut down entirely twice a year, two weeks in summer and one week in winter to allow everyone to truly recharge and to avoid prolonged slowdowns (especially in the summer). These pauses are part of your total vacation time, giving everyone a real chance to unplug and recharge. No Slack, no email, no FOMO.
